back:
Low-level languages (machine code, assembly) provide little abstraction from the CPU. They are fast but not portable, require architecture knowledge, and are hard to write at scale.

High-level languages (C, C++, Java, ...) abstract away the machine. They are easier to read/write, more portable, and take fewer instructions for the same work. C++ is sometimes called mid-level because you can work at both levels.
